The poster presents a strong and convincing evaluation of the Theory of Planned Behaviour, clearly distinguishing between causal and non-causal evidence.The use of graphs and statistical findings to demonstrate the intention-behaviour gap, as well as the separate evaluation of the model's causal claims. The conclusion is balanced and acknowledges that intentions predict behaviour but do not fully explain it. The visual layout is clean, consistent, and easy to follow, with effective use of colours and diagrams. However, the name of the theory is not immediately clear, as the main title is presented as a question rather than explicitly identifying the Theory of Planned Behaviour.

The poster provides an interesting overview of the mind-behaviour gap, using several studies to demonstrate why environmental attitudes and intentions do not always translate into action. The section on the hierarchy of scientific evidence is informative but feels somewhat disconnected from the main topic. Visually, the large amount of small text makes some sections difficult to read. Shorter paragraphs and a clearer distinction between causal and non-causal findings would improve the poster overall. In addition, I think the causal and non-casual should be presented more clearly.
